official_data_replication_seed43.interpretation: Running the audited official probe on the OFFICIAL probing HDF5s reproduces the same low distractor R2. The failure is not caused by the new data, seeds, or action_repeat_prob.

readout_diagnosis.grid_validation_scope: Level 1 only; upper levels are 192-D latents with no spatial tokens. All three model families pass the 0.85 audit with the same probe architecture and 60-epoch budget.
readout_diagnosis.interpretation: The distractor position IS present in the Level-1 patch tokens (4x4-grid linear ridge R2 0.994-0.995) but is discarded by the official CLS pooling. The same 60-epoch two-head probe architecture fed with a 4x4 spatial grid (3072-D) passes the 0.85 audit on both preflight seeds. The bottleneck is the readout, not the encoder or the data.

A_fourroom_probe_v2.rows: L1 4 readouts x 3 seeds x 1 rule; L2 2 readouts x 3 seeds x 2 rules

conclusion: The audited official CLS readout recovers the agent axes almost perfectly at both depths and on both datasets, but recovers the distractor axes only to R2 ~0.4-0.7 at Level 1 and less at Level 2. This is reproducible on the official probing data and is a property of the CLS readout, not the encoder: the distractor is linearly decodable (R2 ~0.99) from a 4x4 spatial grid of the same frozen patch tokens. Proceeding unchanged would make nearly every Wave-1 cell RECOVERY_NOT_VERIFIED; a spatial-grid Level-1 readout passes the audit on both preflight seeds.
